heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1P effortlessly prints Hatchbox PETG out of the box on its stock stainless steel nozzle without requiring an enclosure. Tuning your process to a safe maximum print speed of 167 mm/s respects the 14 mm³/s volumetric flow limit to ensure strong layer adhesion and clean surface finish.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with a thin glue stick layer or liquid release agent to prevent permanent surface bonding.
slicerTweaks: Set Maximum Volumetric Speed to 14 mm³/s in OrcaSlicer filament settings to automatically cap linear extrusion speed around 167 mm/s.
Adjust Pressure Advance (PA) to approximately 0.032 - 0.038 s to eliminate corner bulging on the direct drive extruder.
Enable 'Wipe while retracting' set to 2 mm to minimize PETG oozing and stringing across open travels.
Configure First Layer Temperature to 240°C with bed at 75°C, dropping nozzle to 238°C for subsequent layers to ensure optimal flow without stringing.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe stringing and fine hair-like wisps across travel paths
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG is highly hygroscopic and absorbs ambient moisture quickly, coupled with oozing during non-print moves.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the spool at 65°C for 6 hours; in OrcaSlicer, enable 'Avoid crossing walls' and increase travel speed to 400 mm/s.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: First layer tearing or chunking out PEI coating upon removal
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG has an aggressive chemical bond with PEI, leading to destructive over-adhesion if printed directly without a barrier.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a uniform layer of PVA glue stick or Bambu liquid glue as a sacrificial release agent, and allow the bed to cool below 35°C before removing parts.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Extruder clicking and surface under-extrusion on fast infill moves
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Printing speeds exceeding the 14 mm³/s volumetric melting capacity of the stock hotend at 238°C.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Lower Sparse Infill speed to match the safe ceiling of 167 mm/s and strictly enforce the 14 mm³/s Max Volumetric Flow limit in the filament profile.

faq.question: Can I print Hatchbox PETG on the stock Bambu P1P without an enclosure?
faq.answer: Yes, PETG prints reliably in open-air environments and does not suffer from high shrinkage rates like ABS or ASA, making the open-frame P1P an optimal host.

faq.question: Do I need to upgrade to a hardened steel nozzle for Hatchbox PETG?
faq.answer: No, standard Hatchbox PETG is non-abrasive, so the stock stainless steel nozzle on the P1P is fully compatible and will not suffer premature wear.

faq.question: Why is my PETG print weak and brittle between layers?
faq.answer: Excessive part cooling or printing too fast limits thermal bonding between layers; reduce part cooling fan speed to 20-40% and ensure the nozzle temperature stays around 238°C.

faq.question: What build plate temperature gives the best adhesion without causing warping?
faq.answer: A bed temperature between 75°C and 78°C provides optimal thermal retention above PETG's glass transition temperature to prevent edge curling.
